50523043.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human C-terminal his6-tagged/N-terminal T7 gene leader sequence-tagged LTA4H at 15 degC by ITC method
50523043.references_previous: Alexander, L.; Allen, S.; Bindoff, N. L. Eff. Brief Mindfulness Interv. Acute Pain Exp. Exam. Individ. Differ. 2013, 1, 1–36.

original_paragraph.ITC Measurements: ITC is a method for investigating the thermodynamics of molecular interactions and is most commonly applied to probe the binding interaction between two molecules. It is based on the direct measurement of the heat that is either released or absorbed during a biomolecular binding event. No modification either with fluorescent markers or by immobilization is required. Therefore, ITC allows to investigate the thermodynamics of molecular interactions in the native state27. ITC was performed with a VP-ITC calorimeter (MicroCal Inc., Northampton, MA, USA) equipped with a 1.45 ml sample cell. All measurements were carried out once at three different temperatures (15 °C, 25 °C and 35 °C). The experiments were performed in buffer (50 mM Tris, 50 mM NaCl, pH 8.0) which was supplemented with 3% DMSO for all experiments except those involving Bestatin. In the general setup 50 – 100 μM of LTA4H was presented in the sample cell and titrated with injections of buffer containing RB202 (750 μM) or Bestatin, Captopril or SC57461A at a concentration of 1.5 mM. The limited solubility of ARM1 required a different setup. Therefore, 7 μM ARM1 was presented in the sample cell and titrated with volumes containing 100 μM LTA4H. In either case a first injection of 5 μl during 10 sec was followed by 23 injections of 12 μl during 24 sec all separated by 3 minutes each to ensure full equilibration.
original_paragraph.Control Experiments: For all experimental setups and at every experimental temperature control experiments were performed with identical settings and conditions but with the respective volume that previously contained the protein being replaced by buffer alone. The observed dilution heats were subtracted from the actual experiments. The collected data were analyzed by Origin 7.0 software (MicroCal).
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Figure 2: Calorimetric investigation of the binding of the five selected ligands to LTA4H at 25°C. The buffer (50 mM Tris, 50 mM NaCl pH 8.0) was supplemented with 3% DMSO for all experiments except experiment B. A: 100 μM LTA4H was injected into the cell containing 7 μM ARM1. B, E: 1.5 mM of ligand was injected into 100 μM LTA4H with B: Bestatin, E: SC57461A. C: 300 μM Captopril was injected into 60 μM LTA4H. D: 750 μM RB202 was injected into 50 μM of LTA4H.
